predecessors.note: The page's infobox lists the Liga Federal as the entity preceding it (the table is garbled; the page does not explain the link). The Battle of Cepeda page has the Federal armies of Ramírez and López defeat the Directorship on 1 February 1820 and puts the League's end in 1820.

successors.note: Entre Ríos went back to the provincial alliance under Mansilla, allied to Buenos Aires after taking power (page); Cliopatria's Río de la Plata shape (1811-1833) covers it. Corrientes declared itself an autonomous federated province on 12 October 1821 (page) and Cliopatria likewise keeps it inside the Río de la Plata outline.

capitals.name: Concepción del Uruguay
capitals.note: The infobox names Concepción del Uruguay as the capital; Hereñú occupied it on 23 October 1821. The coordinates are the gazetteer's.

rulers.name: Francisco Ramírez
rulers.title: Governor of Entre Ríos
rulers.note: Listed 1820-1821 in the infobox; killed at the Battle of Chañar Viejo on 10 July 1821, aged 33. The page quotes his 'Proclama del Gobernador de Entre Ríos don Francisco Ramírez'.

rulers.name: José Ricardo López Jordán
rulers.title: Delegate in government, then successor
rulers.note: Ramírez's half-brother and delegate in government, who briefly succeeded him and called indirect elections; he went into exile in Paysandú after Hereñú defeated Piris at Gená on 20 October 1821.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, Cliopatria has no row for the republic (its Río de la Plata shape covers both provinces in 1820 and 1821). The lead puts it on the modern provinces of Entre Ríos and Corrientes with 'approximately 166,980 km2'; the infobox dates it 29 September 1820 to 28 September 1821 and the body has Ramírez occupy Corrientes on 19 September 1820. The two provinces' gazetteer cells cover 847 cells (about 214,000 km2), more than the page's figure, probably because the cells overshoot the rivers. Misiones is left out: the page says only that its commander general was lost after December 1820 and Ramírez appointed local commanders (confidence 2 for the extent: the page gives provinces, not a boundary).

ledger.note: 29 September 1820: the Republic of Entre Ríos is established. Infobox: 'Established: September 29 1820'; Cepeda page: Ramírez 'declared the Republic of Entre Ríos on September 29, 1820.' The land is the modern provinces of Entre Ríos and Corrientes (Ramírez occupied Corrientes on 19 September 1820); the lands come out of the Río de la Plata outline Cliopatria draws.

28 September 1821: Mansilla takes Entre Ríos. Colonel Lucio Norberto Mansilla rebelled in Paraná on 23 September 1821 (backed by Santa Fe, a Buenos Aires squadron under Zapiola and Eusebio Hereñú) and had himself elected governor on 28 September; Hereñú occupied Concepción del Uruguay on 23 October. Entre Ríos then sat with the provincial alliance, Mansilla allied to Buenos Aires.

12 October 1821: Corrientes leaves. Corrientes' civic leaders deposed Carriego and named Nicolás Ramón de Atienza provisional governor; the same day he announced Corrientes' autonomy as a federated province. Ferré's troops reached the city on 18 October. Cliopatria keeps Corrientes inside the Río de la Plata outline, so the counterpart is nominal.

ledger.note: 1821: the Republic of Entre Ríos ends. Infobox: 'Disestablished: 28. September 1821' (the day Mansilla was elected governor); the body ties the end to the October events (Gená 20 October, Concepción del Uruguay occupied 23 October) after which the republic 'was considered dissolved'; Mansilla was elected constitutional governor on 16 December 1821. The page does not reconcile September and October.

wars.name: Battle of Chañar Viejo
belligerents: Santa Fe and Córdoba forces of Estanislao López
wars.outcome: Ramírez was killed on 10 July 1821 near Villa de María de Río Seco and San Francisco del Chañar in Córdoba ('assassinated ... by forces loyal to his former ally López' on the Cepeda page); López Jordán succeeded him and the republic fell by October.
wars.note: The Entre Ríos page does not name the forces or the winner beyond Ramírez's death and says Francisco de Bedoya killed him; the opposing side is taken from the Cepeda page's wording. The page lists no change of border from the battle.

certainty.note: The page names provinces, not a boundary line; Misiones' relation to Ramírez after December 1820 is unclear.

sources.title: Republic of Entre Ríos
sources.note: Infobox dates 29 September 1820 - 28 September 1821, capital, rulers; Corrientes 19 September 1820 and 12 October 1821; Chañar Viejo 10 July 1821; Mansilla's coup.

sources.title: Battle of Cepeda (1820)
sources.note: Ramírez declared the Republic of Entre Ríos on 29 September 1820; assassinated 10 July 1821 by forces loyal to López.

notes: Not in Cliopatria. The Entre Ríos page gives an area (approximately 166,980 km2) and no boundary; the two provinces' gazetteer cells are larger. The infobox end (28 September 1821) and the body (October 1821 events) differ; the page's predecessor and successor boxes are garbled ('United Provinces of South America') and are not used. Misiones' status after 1820 and the republic's relation to Artigas's Federal League are not explained on the page (Ramírez's lieutenants pursued Artigas through Misiones). Corrientes' 12 October 1821 autonomy is read as a loss to the nominal Río de la Plata outline, as Cliopatria draws it.
